title: GENEALOGY RESEARCH CASEBOOK: A Seven-Step Method for Working the Family Evidence
description: Turn family-history questions into organized investigations.Who was this ancestor? Which record is correct? Why do the names, dates, and places disagree? The Genealogy Research Casebook gives family investigators a practical seven-step method for examining evidence, following clues, and reaching carefully supported conclusions.Using the engaging framework of a detective’s case, this 8 × 10 workbook helps you:• Define a focused research question• Plan purposeful searches• Record sources and findings• Build timelines and compare identities• Follow relatives, neighbors, and associates• Evaluate DNA evidence and conflicting information• Test explanations and write a reasoned conclusionBrief instructions appear before each worksheet group, leaving most of the book for actual research. Repeating forms provide generous space for case logs, source evaluations, timelines, identity comparisons, DNA notes, conflicting evidence, research conclusions, and next steps.For the clearest results, use one casebook for a principal family line, ancestral couple, or major research problem—while following collateral relatives and associates whenever they may help solve the case.This casebook does not replace your permanent family tree, pedigree charts, or formal genealogical reports. It preserves the path of your investigation so you can see what you searched, what you found, what remains uncertain, and what to do next.Created by Boyd C. Hemminger after sixty years of family-history research, this is a practical working companion for beginning and experienced family investigators alike.  if(window.mix_csa){window.mix_csa('[cel_widget_id="tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_3"]', '#CardInstanceIvdKrg9zhuL64zgGPWieVw')('mark', 'bb')} if(window.uet){window.uet('bb','tell-amazon-desktop_DetailPage_3',

title: The Big Book of Genealogy Lists
description: Welcome to The Big Book of Genealogy Lists , your essential companion to navigating the often mysterious world of historical documents and family records. Whether you’re a seasoned genealogist or someone just beginning to explore your family roots, you’ve likely encountered puzzling abbreviations, archaic terms, or unfamiliar spellings that can stall your progress. This book is designed to empower you with a convenient collection of reference lists that will transform your research from frustrating to fascinating. As you delve into old census schedules, deeds, court papers, city directories, and weathered headstones, you’ll run across symbols and language that reflect the culture and realities of bygone eras. You may uncover Latin phrases in legal documents, decode city directory abbreviations for occupations that no longer exist, or interpret curious medical causes of death that appear archaic to modern eyes. This is where The Big Book of Genealogy Lists becomes an invaluable tool—each curated list helps you break through these linguistic barriers, bringing clarity and context to your discoveries. Inside these pages, you’ll find: Common Abbreviations & Acronyms used by clerks, census takers, and record-keepers, ensuring you don’t miss critical details in your ancestors’ files. Land & Legal Terminology that can make deciphering deeds, wills, and property records less daunting. Spelling & Phonetic Substitutions , revealing how names and words evolved across regions and generations. City Directory Abbreviations , a treasure trove of insight for locating family members in cities as well as towns settings. title: Genealogy offline
description: Revised edition, September 2014: more images, updated content, and corrected page numbers. Experienced genealogists know that the vast majority of valuable family history records are NOT online, but are housed in libraries, archives, historical societies and courthouses across the nation. After you've found names and dates and some basic information on the internet, where do you go for details? How can you find out how your ancestors lived? In this book Claudia Breland, a professional genealogist with almost 40 years of research experience, will walk you through the basics of obtaining records such as: Social Security Applications Land and Property Records Wills and Probate Records Vital Records Court Records Military Records Divorce Records Adoption and Guardianship Records Newspapers Naturalization Records Each chapter describes the type of record, the information contained, where to find them, and fascinating examples. title: Best AI Prompts for Genealogy Research (2026 Edition)
description: Best AI Prompts for Genealogy Research (2026 Edition) Turn Artificial Intelligence into your most powerful research assistant—without compromising sound genealogy methodology. Artificial intelligence is transforming research—but many genealogists are understandably cautious. After all, family history depends on evidence, sources, and careful analysis. The last thing serious researchers want is a tool that invents answers or shortcuts the work. That’s exactly why this book exists. Best AI Prompts for Genealogy Research (2026 Edition) shows you how to use modern AI tools the right way —as a research assistant that helps you work faster, think more creatively, and analyze records more effectively while still following solid genealogical standards. AI doesn’t replace the genealogist. It amplifies the genealogist. In this practical guide, you’ll learn how to ask AI the right questions so it becomes a powerful partner in your research process. Each chapter focuses on real genealogical tasks and provides ready-to-use prompts you can copy, paste, and adapt in tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and others. title: 10 Tips for Using Historical Maps for Genealogy
description: It is likely that as a genealogist you not only have a love of history and historical records, but also maps. So what is it about this two-dimensional depiction of geography that fascinates us? Perhaps because that very map could be the treasure map to helping us unlock information about our family history and our ancestors. Maps have been around as long as humans needed to remember specific locations. For genealogists, maps are more than just a statement of place: they contain valuable clues for research. Learn the basics of maps and the valuable information they contain for genealogy research. title: Genealogy Standards Second Edition Revised
description: Family historians depend upon thousands of people unknown to them. They exchange research with others; copy information from books and databases; and write libraries, societies, and government offices. At times they even hire professionals to do legwork in distant areas and trust strangers to solve important problems. But how do family historians know they are producing or receiving trustworthy results? This official manual from the Board of Certification for Genealogists, essentially a users' guide for family historians, provides standards for genealogical researchers to assess their own and others' work. The revised second edition increases the clarity of DNA and privacy standards. description: Quillen Does It Again! Professional genealogist and writer Daniel Quillen has done it again. After writing genealogy books for genealogists of all experience levels, he’s focused almost solely on beginning genealogists with his latest book: Beginner’s Guide to Genealogy . If you are a beginner to the passion of genealogy (or even if you have some experience and need more!), this up-to-date, concise, and information-packed book will show you tips and tricks, essential records, and websites you need to know to enable you to begin tracing your ancestors – and be successful!
